title: Happy Students
statement:
A class has `n` students, where `n` is the length of `nums`. A teacher picks a group: any subset of the students, which may be empty or contain everyone. Let `k` be how many students are in the group. Student `i` is happy in exactly two situations:

- they are in the group and `k > nums[i]`, or
- they are left out and `k < nums[i]`.

Return how many different groups (different sets of students) leave every student happy.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all 2^n groups is hopeless, so fix the group size `k` instead. A chosen student needs `nums[i] < k` and a left-out one needs `nums[i] > k`. That forces the group: everyone below `k` must be in it, everyone above `k` must be out, and nobody may equal `k`. So a size `k` gives exactly one valid group when exactly `k` values are below `k` and none equals `k`, and none otherwise. After sorting, that means the `k` smallest values are all below `k` and the next one is above `k`.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order.
2. Try every size `k` from `0` to `n`; the candidate group is the `k` smallest values.
3. If `k > 0` and `nums[k - 1] >= k`, the largest chosen value is not below `k`: skip.
4. If `k < n` and `nums[k] <= k`, the smallest left-out value is not above `k`: skip.
5. Otherwise the group works, so add one to `ways`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 1]` is already sorted and `n = 2`.

- `k = 0`: nobody is chosen and `nums[0] = 1 > 0`, so `ways = 1`.
- `k = 1`: `nums[0] = 1` is not below `1`, so skip.
- `k = 2`: `nums[1] = 1 < 2` and nobody is left out, so `ways = 2`.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan over `k` is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Both comparisons are strict: a student whose value equals `k` is unhappy in or out of a group of size `k`.
- Each valid size is one group, even with duplicate values; do not count combinations.
- Choosing everyone always works because every value is below `n`; the empty group works only when no value is `0`.
- Guard the reads `nums[k - 1]` and `nums[k]` at the two ends of the range.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of students |
| `k` | the group size being tried |
| `ways` | number of group sizes, and so groups, that work |
